intro: Week 10 opens with Kirk Cousins already in a new uniform, the Bengals and Steelers meeting for the AFC North lead on Sunday night, and the Broncos, Bears, Eagles and Buccaneers sitting out on byes. Injuries hit the Vikings, Chargers and 49ers receiving and quarterback rooms hard. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Cousins starts for the Vikings five days after the deadline trade
top.dek: Minnesota sent for Kirk Cousins on deadline day and Kevin O'Connell named him the starter at Lambeau today. Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 for 81 yards with three turnovers in Monday's loss to Buffalo, and Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring injury. Las Vegas gave the job to rookie Fernando Mendoza.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Mike Evans' Achilles injury moves Keenan Allen into the 49ers lineup
top.dek: Evans is sidelined, so Allen, a trade deadline pickup, is expected to play at Dallas today. Left tackle Trent Williams also sat out Friday practice with a shoulder injury and carries no formal designation. Brock Purdy says Allen already knows the plays and formations.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: C.J. Stroud throws five touchdowns in Houston's rout of the Chargers
top.dek: Stroud went 21 of 35 for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception in the 44-22 win. Houston piled up 485 total yards, and Boutte caught two scores for 125 yards. The Texans now chase a third win in four games at Cleveland.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 322: Josh Allen's career touchdowns tie Peyton Manning
top.dek: Allen threw for 234 yards and a 25-yard score to Keleki Latu in Monday's 23-6 win over Minnesota. His 322 regular-season touchdowns, 232 passing, 88 rushing and 2 receiving, match Manning for the most through a player's first 10 years. The 7-1 Bills visit the Jets today.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Steelers visit the Bengals on Sunday night with the AFC North lead at stake
top.dek: Both teams enter 6-2, and kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Cincinnati has won four straight, and Pittsburgh took the first meeting 30-27 on Sept. 27. Watch the Bengals' run defense against Jaylen Warren.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills 7-1, short week at the Jets

stories.text: Bills reach 7-1 and head to MetLife on a short week
stories.summary: Buffalo beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night to match its best eight-game start since 1993. The Bills held the ball for 42:32 and now play the Jets on Sunday with one fewer day of prep than usual.

stories.text: Spencer Brown doubtful, Benford questionable vs Jets
stories.summary: Right tackle Spencer Brown (ankle) did not practice Thursday or Friday and is doubtful, with Tylan Grable next in line. Cornerback Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable but practiced fully Friday, and tight end Dalton Kincaid is cleared.

stories.text: James Cook carries the Bills past Minnesota
stories.summary: Cook ran 31 times for 107 yards and added a late touchdown against the Vikings. He brings 814 rushing yards and 169 carries, third most in the league, into Sunday.

stories.text: 322: Josh Allen's touchdowns tie Peyton Manning
stories.summary: Allen threw for 234 yards and a 25-yard touchdown to Keleki Latu before halftime on Monday. His 322 regular-season touchdowns (232 passing, 88 rushing, 2 receiving) match Manning for the most through a player's first 10 years.

stories.text: At the Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo visits MetLife Stadium for its third AFC East game of the season against a Jets team that is 2-7. Watch whether the Bills can slow Geno Smith's deep passing and keep their offense, the league leader in yards and points per game, on schedule.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: McCord starts as Willis goes to IR

stories.text: Dolphins turn to Kyle McCord after Willis lands on IR
stories.summary: Miami put Malik Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury, and he will miss at least four games. McCord, in his second NFL season, starts at Indianapolis for a team that is 1-7.

stories.text: Sieler done for year, Brewer out vs Colts
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Zach Sieler tore his biceps against Detroit and is on injured reserve. Center Aaron Brewer (concussion) and receiver Jared Wayne are out, receiver Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful and cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee) is questionable.

stories.text: Caleb Douglas gives Miami a bright spot in the passing game
stories.summary: Douglas caught six of eight targets for 70 yards against Detroit. He has 296 receiving yards through five games.

stories.text: 0 for 3: Miami's red zone trips in Detroit
stories.summary: The Dolphins came up empty on all three red zone visits in the 19-9 loss. They also took 11 penalties, missed a field goal and rushed for under 100 yards for the second straight game.

stories.text: At the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami plays at Lucas Oil Stadium against a 2-7 Colts team trying to end a five-game home losing streak. The Dolphins will see how McCord handles his first start of the year behind a defense that held Detroit to 270 yards.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots seek a reset in Munich

stories.text: Patriots fly to Munich to answer a 45-27 loss
stories.summary: New England is 5-4 after Green Bay scored 45, the most points a Patriots defense has allowed in a regular-season game since 1993. The Patriots now face the Lions in Germany with nine players questionable.

stories.text: A.J. Brown and Stevenson questionable for Munich
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) was limited all week and is questionable, as is running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee). Center Ben Brown, cornerback Carlton Davis III and running back TreVeyon Henderson are out.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws for 299 but gives it away three times
stories.summary: Maye went 21 of 38 for 299 yards and three touchdowns against Green Bay, with three first-half interceptions and four sacks. He said he was disappointed in himself.

stories.text: -11: Patriots turnover margin ranks 31st
stories.summary: New England's minus-11 turnover differential ties for 31st in the league, while Detroit sits at plus-3. The Patriots' pass defense ranks 25th, and the Lions' ranks 32nd.

stories.text: Vs. Lions in Munich Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Patriots play Detroit (6-2) at FC Bayern Munich Stadium. Watch whether Maye protects the ball and who is available at receiver and running back.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets host 7-1 Bills on a four-game skid

stories.text: Jets hit the Bills at 2-7 after a 35-12 loss in Kansas City
stories.summary: New York has lost four straight and managed 58 yards after halftime against the Chiefs. Sunday is the last home game before a two-game road trip and the bye.

stories.text: Wilson and Cooper both questionable but practiced fully
stories.summary: Receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) were full participants Friday and are questionable. Linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) is out, and Adonai Mitchell, Harrison Phillips, Joseph Ossai, Nahshon Wright and VJ Payne are also questionable.

stories.text: Rookie David Bailey is wrecking blocks
stories.summary: Bailey returned from a groin injury to post two sacks, three tackles for loss and three QB hits against Kansas City. His 7.5 sacks trail only Will Anderson Jr. (9.5) and Chase Young (8).

stories.text: 100.5: Geno Smith's rating tops Jets QBs since the merger
stories.summary: Smith's passer rating through nine weeks is the best by a Jets quarterback at this point of a season since the merger, with a 100-attempt minimum. He went 18 of 32 for 165 yards in Kansas City and said the red zone struggles frustrate him.

stories.text: Vs. Bills on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Jets host the 7-1 Bills at MetLife Stadium. They need to turn red zone trips into touchdowns and slow Buffalo's run game led by Josh Allen and James Cook.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Brissett gets the call on Monday night

stories.text: Brissett set to start for a Ravens team on a four-game skid
stories.summary: Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett after the Jaguars loss and expects him to start Monday against the winless Chargers. He is an 11-year veteran on his seventh team and calls the prep a crash course. Brissett ranked last among qualified quarterbacks in yards per attempt (5.6) in eight starts with Arizona this year.

stories.text: Jackson's thumb and Hawkins' knee leave Ravens thin
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson suffered a broken and dislocated thumb and is out. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins has been ruled out for Monday night. Baltimore is also on its third kicker of the season, with Riley Patterson signed to the active roster.

stories.text: Henry climbs to seventh on the all-time rushing list
stories.summary: Derrick Henry ran for 57 yards on 17 carries in the 33-10 loss to Jacksonville. He passed Jerome Bettis and LaDainian Tomlinson along the way and now has 13,707 career rushing yards. Curtis Martin sits sixth at 14,101.

stories.text: 104: points the Ravens' defense gave up to three top QBs
stories.summary: Baltimore allowed 104 combined points to the offenses of Joe Burrow, Josh Allen and Trevor Lawrence. Safety Kyle Hamilton said the group is still searching for its identity. The Ravens have lost four straight.

stories.text: Chargers visit Baltimore on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: The Ravens host the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16 at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN. Los Angeles is 0-8, the only winless team in the league. Watch whether Brissett can take pressure off Henry and the run game.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals host Steelers with AFC North lead at stake

stories.text: Bengals and Steelers meet at 6-2 for the division lead
stories.summary: Cincinnati has won four straight, its best start since 2015, and beat Atlanta 31-17 in Madrid last week. Pittsburgh won the first meeting 30-27 on Sept. 27. In five of the previous six first-place meetings between these teams, the winner took the division.

stories.text: Dugger out; Bengals line up several rest-day tackles
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) did not practice all week and is out. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill and Dexter Lawrence carried rest designations, and Allen returned as a limited participant Friday. Guard Dylan Fairchild and cornerback DJ Turner II finished the week as full participants.

stories.text: Burrow leads the league through eight games
stories.summary: Joe Burrow has 2,386 passing yards, 23 touchdowns and six interceptions. Since Week 5 he leads the league with a 77 percent completion rate and 16 touchdown passes. He threw for 282 yards and three scores in the first meeting with Pittsburgh.

stories.text: 5.04: yards per carry the Bengals allow, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Cincinnati's run defense ranks 25th and gives up the highest yards per carry in the league. Steelers back Jaylen Warren leads the NFL at 5.92 yards per carry. Linebackers Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. each have nine missed tackles.

stories.text: Steelers visit Cincinnati on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: The Bengals host Pittsburgh tonight at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. A win would split the season series. Watch the Bengals' run defense against Warren.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Watson returns as Browns host Texans

stories.text: Browns hand the job back to Watson for Texans game
stories.summary: Coach Todd Monken reportedly named Deshaun Watson the starter over Shedeur Sanders for Sunday. Watson missed Week 9 after entering concussion protocol. The Browns are 5-3 with Watson starting and lost the Saints game in overtime with Sanders.

stories.text: Boston questionable; Hickman and Burton out
stories.summary: Wide receiver Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable after returning as a limited participant Friday. Safety Ronnie Hickman (concussion) and fullback Michael Burton (calf) are out. Monken said Boston is trending in the right direction.

stories.text: Sanders put up 297 yards in his first start
stories.summary: Shedeur Sanders went 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the overtime loss at New Orleans. He threw for 197 yards and both scores in the fourth quarter and overtime, with no interceptions on the year. He goes back to backup duty this week.

stories.text: 38: sacks Cleveland has allowed through nine games
stories.summary: Watson has taken 33 of them and Sanders five. The Browns' 40.5 percent pressure rate allowed ranks second in the NFL. Houston has 29 sacks in eight games.

stories.text: Texans visit Cleveland on Sunday at 1 PM
stories.summary: The Browns host Houston today at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. Forecast calls for cool temperatures and a chance of light rain. A win would send Cleveland into its bye at 6-4.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers bring four-game streak to Cincinnati

stories.text: Steelers chase the AFC North lead off a bye week
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-2 and has won four straight and five of its last six. The Steelers beat Cincinnati 30-27 on Sept. 27, and Derrick Harmon's strip-sack on the Bengals' final drive sealed it. Mike Tomlin, now an NBC analyst, sees his former team in person for the first time since leaving.

stories.text: Harmon questionable; Watt and Heyward back to full
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon (foot) is questionable and is on injured reserve with a designation to return. T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and Darnell Washington had rest days and ended the week as full participants. The Steelers held a walkthrough Friday, so those statuses are estimates.

stories.text: Warren leads the NFL at 5.92 yards per carry
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren had 176 all-purpose yards in the Week 3 win over Cincinnati. He has topped 100 rushing yards in three of the five games since, including a season-high 143 against Cleveland. The Steelers average 145.7 rushing yards over their last three games.

stories.text: 85: Aaron Rodgers' Sunday night touchdown passes
stories.summary: That is the most of any quarterback, per the Fox Sports preview. Pittsburgh also has 18 Sunday night road wins, tied for second most. The Steelers have 26 sacks this season, tied for fourth in the league.

stories.text: Steelers at Bengals on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits Cincinnati tonight at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. Watch whether the Steelers' pass rush, with 26 sacks this season, can pressure Joe Burrow.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans chase a third win in four at Cleveland

stories.text: Texans climb out of 0-4 hole, now eye Cleveland
stories.summary: Houston opened 0-4 and has won three of its last four. Last week the Texans beat the winless Chargers 44-22, with eight sacks from the defense. They carry that momentum into Cleveland today.

stories.text: Hunter, Al-Shaair, Harrison out; Anderson questionable
stories.summary: Houston ruled out Danielle Hunter, Azeez Al-Shaair, receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), lineman Keylan Rutledge and tight end Brevin Jordan. Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) and right tackle Trent Brown (illness, wrist) are questionable. David Montgomery (groin) moved to full participation.

stories.text: Stroud throws five touchdowns in rout of Chargers
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud went 21 of 35 for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception in the 44-22 win on Nov. 8. Houston piled up 485 total yards. Boutte caught two touchdowns for 125 yards, and Tank Dell added 105 yards and a score.

stories.text: 9.5: Will Anderson Jr.'s sacks lead the NFL
stories.summary: Anderson leads the league with 9.5 sacks, and the Texans are tied with Minnesota for the most team sacks. His ankle is the question today. He left Thursday's practice and sat out Friday.

stories.text: At Cleveland, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Houston visits the Browns today at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. The forecast in Cleveland calls for mid 40s, a northwest wind and a chance of light rain. Watch how the Texans protect without Brown at full strength and how they cover for Al-Shaair in the middle.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts sell four vets, keep Taylor, host Miami

stories.text: Colts trade four vets, own 10 picks in 2027
stories.summary: At Tuesday's deadline Indianapolis sent Quenton Nelson to Seattle, DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen to San Francisco, and Josh Downs to Kansas City. The team now holds 10 picks in the 2027 draft and eight in 2028. General manager Chris Ballard was dismissed in October.

stories.text: Six Colts out against Miami, Walley and Key trending up
stories.summary: Tight end Mo Alie-Cox, linebackers Jaylon Carlies and Akeem Davis-Gaither, long snapper Luke Rhodes, tackle Jerry Tillery and right tackle Jalen Travis are out. Cornerback Justin Walley and edge Arden Key are trending toward playing.

stories.text: Daniel Jones throws late pick in loss to Dallas
stories.summary: Jones went 20 of 34 for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Caleb Downs picked him off with 35 seconds left, after Spencer Shrader's 50-yard field goal put Indianapolis ahead 23-20. Ashton Dulin caught a 55-yard touchdown on a screen.

stories.text: 508: yards Dallas gained on the Colts defense
stories.summary: Dallas piled up 508 yards in a 27-23 win, and CeeDee Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards. It was the Colts' fifth straight loss and their 14th in 16 games. The Colts managed 180 passing yards on 34 attempts.

stories.text: Home against Miami, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Colts host the Dolphins today at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Miami is down to one win and starts Kyle McCord at quarterback with Malik Willis on injured reserve. Indianapolis is thin at receiver after the Allen and Downs trades, so Tyler Warren and the run game carry the load.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lead the South, visit Titans today

stories.text: Jaguars beat Ravens 33-10, lead South by three games
stories.summary: Jacksonville moved to 6-2 with a Thursday night win in Baltimore. The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 319 to 227 and forced three turnovers. They have scored 31 or more in each of their last three games.

stories.text: Bates and Davis rest, Green out, Hainsey questionable
stories.summary: Safety Jessie Bates III and tackle Jordan Davis are out for rest, not injury. Edge BJ Green II (forearm) is out. Lineman Robert Hainsey (concussion) is questionable.

stories.text: Lawrence posts the NFL's second best passer rating
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence has 18 touchdown passes and four interceptions, with a 111.7 passer rating that ranks second in the league. Last week he went 16 of 26 for 242 yards and a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington.

stories.text: +108: Jaguars scoring margin leads the NFL
stories.summary: Jacksonville is the only team with a top-five scoring offense and a top-five scoring defense. The Jaguars score 28.6 points a game and allow 15.1. They are only the fourth team since 2000 to win four of their first eight games by 23 or more points.

stories.text: At Tennessee, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Jaguars play at Nissan Stadium today at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. Jacksonville has beaten Tennessee four straight times. The rematch is Nov. 29 in Jacksonville.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans host first-place Jaguars after the bye

stories.text: Titans trade safety Hooker to Buffalo for a 2027 second
stories.summary: Tennessee sent Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Bills for a 2027 second-round pick. Hooker had five interceptions this season and 17 for his career. The Titans now hold two first-round and two second-round picks in 2027.

stories.text: Five Titans out, Spears questionable vs Jaguars
stories.summary: Receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), linebackers Anthony Hill Jr. (neck) and Cody Barton (concussion), and punter Tommy Townsend are out. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) practiced fully and is questionable. Cedric Gray is expected to play the full game at linebacker.

stories.text: Pollard rides back to back 100 yard games
stories.summary: Tony Pollard has 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns this season. He ran for 117 yards and two scores in the overtime loss at Cincinnati, his second straight 100 yard game. He has five touchdowns over the last two games.

stories.text: 86-3: Titans second quarter deficit through eight games
stories.summary: Opponents have outscored Tennessee 86-3 in the second quarter. The Titans have outscored teams 47-27 in the first quarter and 70-47 in the fourth. They have scored 65.3 percent of their points in the second half or overtime.

stories.text: Home against Jacksonville, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Titans host the Jaguars today at 1:00 PM ET on FOX, coming off their bye. Tennessee has no home win this season, and its only win came at Indianapolis on Oct. 18. The rematch is Nov. 29 in Jacksonville.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos 7-2 and resting on a bye

stories.text: Broncos enter the bye at 7-2 on a five-game streak
stories.summary: Denver beat Carolina 26-21 in Week 9 and sits second in the AFC, tied with Buffalo, San Francisco and Chicago for the most wins in the league. Sean Payton's teams are 4-0 in the last game before a bye. Bo Nix said the group feels confident but sees plenty to clean up.

stories.text: Safeties and Moss are the bye-week health watch
stories.summary: Starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones missed the Carolina game, and cornerback Riley Moss left it hurt. JL Skinner and Jahdae Barron played 112 combined snaps in the secondary. The bye gives all three time before the Raiders visit in Week 11.

stories.text: Nik Bonitto ends the Panthers game with a strip-sack
stories.summary: Bonitto faked inside, beat left tackle Rasheed Walker outside and ripped the ball from Bryce Young on Carolina's last snap, then fell on it. The play sealed a 26-21 win with 1:24 left. Denver has 26 sacks through nine games.

stories.text: 16: straight one-score wins, an NFL record
stories.summary: The Broncos passed the 2008-09 Colts with the Carolina win, their 16th consecutive regular-season game decided by one score and won. The run started with a comeback in Philadelphia. Six of Denver's seven wins this year came by seven points or fewer.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then the Raiders at home in Week 11
stories.summary: Denver is off this weekend and returns Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS against Las Vegas, which will start rookie Fernando Mendoza by then. Watch the third-down numbers: the offense converts 29.7%, worst in the league.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs at Atlanta without Walker

stories.text: Chiefs go to Atlanta at 6-2 with Walker sidelined
stories.summary: Kansas City bounced back from its Denver loss with a 35-12 win over the Jets and now visits the Falcons. Running back Kenneth Walker III is out with a groin injury, and Andy Reid said the team will not put him at risk. Rookie Emmett Johnson is set to carry the load.

stories.text: Mahomes practices fully, Moore and Woods are out
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes took a hit to his right elbow against the Jets and was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) are out. Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and back Jaydn Ott (hamstring) are questionable, and Xavier Worthy is expected to play.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker III has 872 yards, second in the NFL
stories.summary: Walker scored three touchdowns in the win over the Jets and ranks second in the league in rushing yards. His groin injury leaves a big hole in the backfield on Sunday.

stories.text: 26.3%: Chiefs pressure-to-sack rate against the Jets
stories.summary: Kansas City sacked the Jets five times, a season high. Its pressure-to-sack rate jumped from 9.8% through Week 8, the lowest in the league, to 26.3% in that game. Atlanta's offense completes only 18% of throws when Michael Penix Jr. is pressured.

stories.text: At Atlanta on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Chiefs play the 3-6 Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Atlanta's Bijan Robinson leads the league in rushing, and the Falcons have allowed 120 or more rushing yards in four of their last five games. Kansas City has topped 150 on the ground five times this season.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza starts vs the NFL's top defense

stories.text: Raiders trade Cousins and hand the job to Mendoza
stories.summary: General manager John Spytek sent Kirk Cousins to Minnesota for a third-round pick and named the No. 1 overall pick the starter. Cousins went 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine starts. Spytek said the move does not mean the team is giving up on a 4-5 season.

stories.text: Booker and Thornton are questionable against Seattle
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) went from limited to full on Friday. Receiver Dont'e Thornton (back) did not practice Friday. Guard Trey Zuhn cleared concussion testing with a full practice and carries no designation.

stories.text: Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker lead the linebacker room
stories.summary: Dean and Walker have combined for 170 tackles, the most of any duo in the NFL. Both anchor a defense that will face a Seattle offense led by backup Drew Lock, with Sam Darnold out.

stories.text: 244.2: yards per game Seattle allows, the NFL's best
stories.summary: Mendoza's debut comes against a Seahawks defense that has not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 38 straight games. He is the fifth No. 1 overall quarterback to start in Week 10 or later, and the previous four all lost their first starts.

stories.text: Seattle at Allegiant on Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts the 5-4 Seahawks, who are without Sam Darnold, Charles Cross, Quenton Nelson and Leonard Williams. The Raiders then face Denver in Week 11. Watch whether Las Vegas can run, since it has topped 100 rushing yards only twice this year.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers visit Baltimore Monday

stories.text: Chargers fall to 0-8 after a 44-22 loss to Houston
stories.summary: The defense gave up a season-high 485 yards and two 63-yard touchdowns. Jim Harbaugh said the team will keep fighting and that every loss hurts. The offense scored three field goals and no touchdowns on its first four drives.

stories.text: Herbert's X-rays are negative, McConkey is day-to-day
stories.summary: Justin Herbert hurt his left hand late against Houston and Harbaugh expects him to play. Ladd McConkey (back spasms) did not practice Friday, along with Trey Pipkins, Branson Taylor and Brenen Thompson. David Njoku and Denzel Perryman are in their 21-day practice windows.

stories.text: Marlowe Wax plays a season-high 22 snaps
stories.summary: Wax had eight tackles and broke up the pass that led to the Chargers' only takeaway. Pro Football Focus graded him 91.3 among Week 9 linebackers, one bright spot in a game that got away.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Justin Herbert, a career high
stories.summary: Houston sacked Herbert eight times and had 17 run stops. Herbert has 1,591 passing yards, six touchdowns and 11 interceptions this season, with Omarion Hampton the team leader at 369 rushing yards.

stories.text: At Baltimore on Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: The Chargers visit a 4-5 Ravens team that has lost four straight and is starting Jacoby Brissett with Lamar Jackson on injured reserve. Baltimore has scored fewer than 14 points in four straight games. Los Angeles is still looking for its first win.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys need back-to-back wins vs 49ers

stories.text: Cowboys try for a first back-to-back win against the 49ers
stories.summary: Dallas sits at 4-5 and 1-3 at home after beating Indianapolis 27-23 last Sunday. A win over San Francisco would give the Cowboys consecutive victories for the first time this season. The 49ers arrive at 7-1, and this is the first of three straight home games, with Tennessee and Philadelphia on Thanksgiving to follow.

stories.text: Pickens, Overshown and Turpin cleared; Porter and Bland questionable
stories.summary: George Pickens (hamstring), DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring and back) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) came off the injury report Friday and will play. Safety P.J. Locke is out with a concussion, and safety Juanyeh Thomas is doubtful. Cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. and DaRon Bland, both with ankle injuries, are questionable. Running back Tyler Goodson went on injured reserve Saturday with a knee injury.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb: 70 catches, 904 yards, 7 touchdowns
stories.summary: Lamb is the first problem San Francisco has to solve. He has 70 catches for 904 yards and seven touchdowns through nine games. Dak Prescott has thrown for 2,381 yards, 16 touchdowns and 5 interceptions, and he has to get the ball out before the 49ers pressure arrives.

stories.text: 153: penalty yards Dallas gave away in a win over the Colts
stories.summary: The Cowboys took 14 penalties for 153 yards and lost two fumbles against Indianapolis, and still won 27-23. They outgained the Colts 508 yards to 271. Dallas converts 45.3 percent of its third downs on the season, 53 of 117.

stories.text: 49ers at AT&T Stadium, Sunday 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Dallas hosts San Francisco today in Arlington, 3:25 p.m. Central on FOX. The 49ers own the best record in the NFC at 7-1. The Cowboys then host Tennessee on Nov. 22 and Philadelphia on Thanksgiving. Watch how Dallas handles a secondary that is thin at safety and uncertain at corner.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants fall to Commanders, still lead East

stories.text: Late Diggs touchdown sends Giants to a 24-21 loss
stories.summary: Washington scored the winner on Jayden Daniels' 32-yard pass to Stefon Diggs with under a minute left. The Giants hold a 5-3-1 record and still lead the NFC East, with Washington at 3-5-1. J.J. McCarthy's late interception to Rasul Douglas ended the Giants' last chance. Their next three games are Jacksonville, San Francisco and Seattle.

stories.text: Skattebo returns from hamstring injury, runs for two scores
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo played after a week off with a hamstring strain and finished with 18 carries for 78 yards and two touchdowns. Kayvon Thibodeaux and Bryan Hudson were evaluated for concussions during the game and cleared.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely: nine catches, 127 yards and a 66-yard score
stories.summary: Likely led the Giants through the air with nine catches for 127 yards and a 66-yard touchdown from McCarthy. It was the longest touchdown reception of his career. McCarthy threw for a career-high 293 yards in the loss.

stories.text: 399: net yards for the Giants, 59 more than Washington
stories.summary: New York outgained Washington 399 to 340 and still lost. The Giants missed a field goal and committed two turnovers. Dominic Zvada's 33-yard attempt went wide left with 4:08 left.

stories.text: Jaguars at MetLife, Sunday Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Giants host Jacksonville, which sits at 6-2 after a 33-10 win at Baltimore and leads the AFC South. The game was moved from 1 p.m. to the 4:25 p.m. window. The Giants are 4-4 all-time against the Jaguars. Watch how the Giants respond after a loss that cost them a game in the division race.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles hit the bye at 2-7 after seventh straight loss

stories.text: Eagles lose a seventh straight, longest skid since 2012
stories.summary: The Giants beat Philadelphia 19-11 at the Linc, dropping the Eagles to 2-7. Rookie Joe Milton III made his first start, threw for 169 yards with no touchdowns and was sacked seven times. Saquon Barkley scored the only touchdown and ran for 22 yards on 13 carries. The Eagles now use their Week 10 bye.

stories.text: Baun left with a back injury; Smith and Wicks out again
stories.summary: Linebacker Zack Baun left the Giants game in the third quarter with a back injury after recording two sacks. Receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) missed a third straight game. Kicker Jake Elliott played through an ankle injury and hit a 45-yard field goal late.

stories.text: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. posts 10 tackles and a forced fumble
stories.summary: Trotter started in place of Jihaad Campbell and made 10 tackles, three tackles for loss, a QB hit and a forced fumble against the Giants. The linebacker group was the best part of a defense that held New York to 80 rushing yards. It was the first game this season the Eagles held an opponent under 100 on the ground.

stories.text: 7: sacks Joe Milton took in his first NFL start
stories.summary: Milton went down seven times for 41 yards against a Giants defense that had nine sacks coming in. He was 18 of 34 for 169 yards and led the team with 64 rushing yards. The offensive line drew an F from NBC10, and rookie right tackle Markel Bell continued to struggle.

stories.text: Bye this week, then Steelers on Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Eagles are off in Week 10. They host Pittsburgh at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. on CBS. The Steelers are 6-2 and have won four straight, including a 27-6 win over Cleveland. The Eagles then play at Dallas on Thanksgiving, Nov. 26, at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Diggs TD lifts Commanders past Giants 24-21

stories.text: Daniels shakes off two picks, Diggs wins it with 57 seconds left
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions while Washington trailed 21-17, then hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The 24-21 win moved Washington to 3-5-1 and keeps their season alive. The Commanders hold the head-to-head edge on New York at 1-0-1, though their playoff odds sit near 19 percent.

stories.text: Okonkwo leaves with back injury; McLaurin still out
stories.summary: Tight end Chig Okonkwo missed much of Thursday's game with a back injury. Terry McLaurin and Jacory Croskey-Merritt did not play.

stories.text: Sonny Styles leads Washington with 13 tackles
stories.summary: Styles made 13 tackles, five of them solo, and one tackle for loss against the Giants. Frankie Luvu forced a Malik Nabers fumble that Jeremy Reaves recovered, the first fumble recovery of Reaves' career. Dan Quinn's challenge also overturned a Giants first down late and forced a punt.

stories.text: 7 of 14: Washington's third-down conversions against the Giants
stories.summary: The Commanders converted seven of 14 third downs while holding New York to four of 12. Daniels had thrown no interceptions through eight games before the two late ones, and he is now 4-0-1 against the Giants in his career. Washington was flagged only four times for 17 yards.

stories.text: Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23, at Northwest Stadium
stories.summary: Washington gets extra rest before hosting Cincinnati on Monday, Nov. 23. Kickoff time and network were not stated in the sources reviewed. Watch whether the offense can keep converting on third down and protect Daniels.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears reach the bye at 7-2 and in first

stories.text: Bears hit the bye 7-2 despite five turnovers
stories.summary: Chicago beat Tampa Bay 27-24 on Sunday night while giving the ball away five times, and it sits first in the NFC North on a four-game win streak. The Bears have 17 giveaways and a turnover margin of minus-four, so the bye is a chance to clean that up. They are 0-2 in the division, with losses to Minnesota and Green Bay.

stories.text: Kmet done for year, Burden and Williams get a week
stories.summary: Tight end Cole Kmet is out for the season, and Colston Loveland has taken over the role. Wide receiver Luther Burden III left the Tampa Bay game with a concussion and has the bye to recover. Caleb Williams is resting a hamstring, and running back Kyle Monangai (toe) is expected back for the Saints.

stories.text: Simmons has a sack in both games as a Bear
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons came over at the trade deadline and has a sack in each of his first two games in Chicago. The Bears are 2-0 with him. He joins a front that has recorded at least two sacks in every game this season.

stories.text: 22.8%: Bears hold opponents to the lowest third-down rate
stories.summary: Opponents convert just 22.8 percent of their third downs against Chicago, the lowest rate in the league by a wide margin. The Bears have also outscored opponents 59-0 in the first quarter of their last six wins.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then the Saints at Soldier Field
stories.summary: Chicago is off this week. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 22 against New Orleans at Soldier Field, kickoff 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Thanksgiving at Detroit follows four days later.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions chase a fifth straight win in Munich

stories.text: Lions play the Patriots in Munich on a four-game streak
stories.summary: Detroit is 6-2 and unbeaten in the NFC North as it faces New England at 9:30 a.m. ET in Germany. A win would tie the Lions with first-place Chicago at 7-2, with Detroit holding the tiebreaker. The Lions have not played the Bears yet.

stories.text: Mays, Joseph and Reed out; St. Brown questionable
stories.summary: Center Cade Mays (ankle), safety Kerby Joseph (knee) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) are out. Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) are questionable. Jared Goff (chest) practiced fully Thursday and Friday with no designation.

stories.text: Gibbs brings 847 rushing yards and nine scores to Munich
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs has 847 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, plus 34 catches for 285 yards. He is the main threat for a Lions offense that must work around the loss of Mays at center.

stories.text: 7: sacks Goff has taken in the last two games
stories.summary: Goff has been sacked seven times over the last two games, and Detroit now plays without center Cade Mays. New England linebacker Elijah Ponder leads the Patriots with 7.5 sacks.

stories.text: Patriots in Munich, 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Detroit faces New England today, kickoff 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX in Munich. Watch how the Lions protect Goff without Mays, and how they handle a Patriots offense led by Drake Maye, who has thrown 11 interceptions.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers host Vikings without Jacobs and Parsons

stories.text: Packers ride a 45-27 rout into the Vikings game
stories.summary: Green Bay beat New England 45-27 on Nov. 8 and has won five of its last six. The Packers forced four turnovers and sacked Drake Maye four times. Now they host a Minnesota team coming off two straight losses.

stories.text: Parsons and Jacobs out against the Vikings
stories.summary: Edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) is out and remains on the physically unable to perform list. Running back Josh Jacobs (finger) is out, along with center Sean Rhyan and tight end Josh Whyle. Safety Xavier McKinney (foot) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back) are questionable.

stories.text: Watson and Golden both set career highs
stories.summary: Christian Watson caught 7 passes for 171 yards and Matthew Golden had 10 for 164 against New England. Both set career highs in receiving yards. It was the fourth time Green Bay has had two receivers with at least 150 yards in one game.

stories.text: 372: Love's passing yards at New England
stories.summary: Jordan Love went 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns for a 153.2 passer rating. He also rushed for a score. His touchdown pass to Golden was the 100th of his career.

stories.text: Vikings at Lambeau, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Minnesota today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Vikings won the Week 1 meeting 39-22. Watch whether Kaleb Johnson carries the run game with Jacobs out.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Cousins starts for Vikings five days after trade

stories.text: Cousins to start at Green Bay after deadline trade
stories.summary: Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on deadline day, and Kevin O'Connell named him the starter for today's game at Lambeau. Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 for 81 yards with three turnovers in the Monday night loss to Buffalo. Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring injury.

stories.text: Murray, Hockenson and Jennings out at Green Bay
stories.summary: Quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf), linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) and lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle) are out. Jordan Addison (thumb), Kyle Van Noy (calf) and Joshua Metellus (shoulder) are questionable.

stories.text: Aaron Jones leads the Vikings with 474 rush yards
stories.summary: Jones has 474 rushing yards on 115 carries and faces his former team on Sunday. He will lean on the run game with Cousins starting five days after the trade.

stories.text: 31st: Vikings offense in yards, 1st defense in points
stories.summary: Minnesota's offense ranks 27th in points and 31st in yards, while its defense ranks first in points allowed and second in yards allowed. That gap explains a 6-2 record and why the front office went and got a quarterback.

stories.text: At Packers, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Minnesota plays at Lambeau Field today, kickoff 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Vikings won the Week 1 meeting 39-22 and can win three straight in the series. Watch how Cousins handles a Green Bay defense playing without Micah Parsons.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons trade Bates, host Chiefs after Madrid loss

stories.text: Falcons trade Jessie Bates III to Jacksonville
stories.summary: Atlanta sent the safety to the Jaguars for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. DeMarcco Hellams is slated to start in his place. The Falcons are 3-6 after a 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, and they need six wins in their last eight for a first winning record since 2017.

stories.text: Branch out, Deablo doubtful for Chiefs
stories.summary: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) is out. Linebacker Divine Deablo is doubtful after aggravating a forearm fracture against the Bengals. Gervon Dexter Sr. (illness) and James Pearce Jr. (back) are both questionable.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson gets back to 100 yards
stories.summary: Robinson ran 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown against Cincinnati and added six catches for 47 yards. It was his first 100-yard game and first rushing score since Oct. 5. The team site lists his total at 147 yards and his fifth rushing touchdown of 2026.

stories.text: 12: Penalties the Falcons took in Madrid
stories.summary: Atlanta set a season high with 12 penalties for 88 yards in the loss. Holding calls on Taylor and Terrell wiped out a first down and a sack. Coach Kevin Stefanski called the flags self-inflicted.

stories.text: Falcons host the Chiefs today at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Atlanta plays Kansas City at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt on the call. The Chiefs come in 6-2 after a 35-12 win over the Jets. Watch whether Atlanta cleans up the penalties against a team coming off a blowout win.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers and Saints play for the NFC South lead

stories.text: Panthers chase NFC South lead at New Orleans
stories.summary: Carolina and New Orleans are both 3-5, so the winner takes first place in the division. The Panthers have lost three straight, the latest a 26-21 defeat to Denver. They have played one division game so far, going 1-1.

stories.text: Okereke out again, Phillips and Lee in question
stories.summary: Linebacker Bobby Okereke is ruled out for the Saints game. Guard Damien Lewis is cleared. Two players were listed questionable on Friday, and the team site links them to Jaelan Phillips and rookie cornerback Will Lee. Brady Christensen is in the second week of his 21-day practice window.

stories.text: Bryce Young shreds Denver on in-breakers
stories.summary: Young went 28 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns against the Broncos, a 106.4 passer rating. He was 13 of 14 for 152 yards and a score on in-breaking routes, per Next Gen Stats. He was strip sacked on the final possession.

stories.text: 4th: Carolina's rank in passing offense
stories.summary: The Panthers average 261.1 passing yards a game, fourth in the NFL, and 362.4 total yards, eighth. The defense gives up 27.4 points a game, tied for 28th.

stories.text: Panthers at Saints today, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The game is at Caesars Superdome, with Kevin Kugler, Daryl Johnston and Allison Williams on the call. New Orleans won the last meeting 20-17 on a 47-yard field goal with two seconds left. The teams meet again Dec. 13 in Charlotte.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints win in OT, host Panthers for first place

stories.text: Waiver claim Estime starts for Saints, wins in OT
stories.summary: Audric Estime was waived by Cleveland on Monday, claimed by New Orleans on Tuesday and starting by Sunday. He ran three times for 32 yards on the opening plays and scored a goal-line touchdown in the fourth quarter. The Saints beat the Browns 23-22 in overtime, and a win over Carolina would put them in first place.

stories.text: Center Erik McCoy left with a biceps injury
stories.summary: McCoy left late in the fourth quarter against Cleveland with a biceps injury, and his status had not been confirmed. Kelvin Banks Jr. returned from an ankle absence and Jordyn Tyson made his season debut. Saints.com listed four players out and two questionable on the Friday report.

stories.text: Carl Granderson piles up sacks
stories.summary: Granderson had two sacks against Cleveland and Chase Young added one, as the Saints totaled five. Both were named NFL sack leaders after Week 9, per the article. Tyler Shough threw for 265 yards and ran for 51 more.

stories.text: 29th: Saints rank in total defense
stories.summary: New Orleans allows 370.5 yards a game, 29th in the league, and 27.0 points a game, 27th. The offense averages 23.1 points, 15th. The Saints are minus-6 in turnover margin.

stories.text: Saints host Panthers today, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The game is at Caesars Superdome, and both teams are 3-5. The Saints lead the all-time series 33-29 and have won two straight against Carolina. They won the Dec. 2025 meeting 20-17.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs on bye, trying to fix the passing game

stories.text: Bucs use bye to fix Mayfield and the pass game
stories.summary: Tampa Bay lost 27-24 at Chicago on a field goal as time expired after leading 14-0. Coach Todd Bowles said offensive coordinator Zac Robinson will keep calling plays. Mayfield was sacked four times and threw two interceptions in the loss.

stories.text: Winfield hurt his ankle against the Bears
stories.summary: Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. hurt his right ankle in the second quarter at Chicago after colliding with Calijah Kancey, and did not return. As of Nov. 10 the team had given no timeline. Ifeatu Melifonwu took his snaps, and the bye gives him until Nov. 22 to heal.

stories.text: Baker Mayfield owns the Chicago loss
stories.summary: Mayfield was sacked four times and threw two interceptions in the Sunday night loss at Soldier Field. He missed three games earlier this season with a dislocated right thumb. The Bucs led 14-0 and forced a season-high five takeaways but still lost.

stories.text: 158.1: Tampa Bay's passing yards per game
stories.summary: That ranks 32nd in the NFL, and the Bucs average 5.9 yards per attempt, 29th. The team is 3-6, a half game out of the NFC South lead.

stories.text: Bucs are on bye, then visit Detroit Nov. 22
stories.summary: Tampa Bay does not play in Week 10. The Bucs visit the Lions at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 22. Detroit is 6-2 after a 19-9 win over Miami.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Rookie Carson Beck makes first NFL start vs. Rams

stories.text: Carson Beck gets the call at quarterback against the Rams
stories.summary: Coach Mike LaFleur confirmed Wednesday that Beck, a third-round rookie, will make his NFL debut Sunday. Arizona benched Jacoby Brissett on Nov. 1 and traded him to Baltimore, then lost Gardner Minshew to a season-ending elbow injury after the Week 9 loss in Seattle. Beck's last game action was the Hall of Fame Game, where he went 15-for-19 before a rib injury ended his preseason.

stories.text: Cardinals enter Rams game with three ruled out and six questionable
stories.summary: Center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), Jon Gaines II (ankle) and Zach Carter (knee) are out. Hunter Long, Roy Lopez, Max Melton, Darius Robinson, Jayden Williams and Dewey Wingard are questionable. Michael Wilson fractured a vertebra against Seattle but will not need surgery, and Hayden Conner is expected to start at center.

stories.text: Trey McBride is the one proven target left for Beck
stories.summary: McBride caught seven passes for 54 yards in the 17-3 loss at Seattle, the most receptions on the team. Wilson, Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks have all suffered season-ending injuries in the past three weeks, so the tight end carries the passing game into Sunday. Seattle stopped a fourth-and-goal throw to McBride from the 2-yard line in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 10: straight home losses, a franchise record for Arizona
stories.summary: The Cardinals have dropped ten consecutive home games, the longest such streak in team history. They host the Rams at State Farm Stadium Sunday, and the Rams are double-digit favorites per the preview. Arizona did beat Los Angeles 18-16 in Week 6 at SoFi Stadium.

stories.text: Rams visit Glendale Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Los Angeles in a divisional rematch. Watch Beck's first series and whether a line missing Paris Johnson Jr., Froholdt and Gaines can hold up against Myles Garrett and the Rams' front. Arizona is a unanimous underdog for the eighth time in 10 games.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams chase a fourth straight win in Arizona

stories.text: Rams try to win without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams
stories.summary: Nacua (MCL and PCL sprains, turf toe) is out for an extended stretch, expected to miss at least four games. Adams (hamstring) is on injured reserve, and Sean McVay called a Week 12 return against Green Bay realistic. The Rams beat Washington 20-13 last Sunday for their third straight win, and a win in Arizona would carry them into the bye on a four-game streak.

stories.text: McDuffie, Garrett and Curl all questionable for Arizona
stories.summary: Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing the Washington game, and McVay said he is optimistic. Myles Garrett (knee) did not practice Friday but McVay sounded hopeful, and Kam Curl (toe) is also questionable. Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and Steve Avila (hamstring) are out.

stories.text: Myles Garrett wrecks Washington in his first game back
stories.summary: Garrett returned from knee surgery after missing seven games and recorded three sacks, a forced fumble, three quarterback hits and three tackles for loss. His third sack came with 2:31 left, and Byron Young then recovered the fumble that sealed the 20-13 win. He had played only the season opener for Los Angeles before the injury.

stories.text: 0-for-9: Rams on third down before they finally converted
stories.summary: Los Angeles missed on its first nine third-down tries at Washington and converted for the first time with 2:48 left in the third quarter. Matthew Stafford finished with 228 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception while playing through an elbow issue. Stafford targeted Nacua 19 times, and Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards.

stories.text: At Arizona Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, then a bye
stories.summary: The Rams play the Cardinals at State Farm Stadium Sunday. Arizona won 18-16 in the first meeting in Week 6, so the Rams will want revenge against a rookie quarterback making his first start. After the Week 11 bye, Los Angeles hosts Green Bay in Week 12.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers at Dallas with Keenan Allen added at receiver

stories.text: Mike Evans' Achilles injury pushes Keenan Allen into the lineup
stories.summary: Evans is sidelined with an Achilles injury, and Allen, acquired at the trade deadline, is expected to play Sunday in Dallas. Allen has 40 catches for 351 yards and a touchdown this season and nearly signed with San Francisco in the offseason before landing in Indianapolis. Brock Purdy said Allen already understands the plays and formations.

stories.text: Trent Williams missed Friday practice with a shoulder injury
stories.summary: The left tackle was limited Thursday and sat out Friday, with no formal designation listed in the report. Dre Greenlaw (knee), Renardo Green (back), Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Upton Stout (shoulder and neck) are questionable. Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) were full participants Friday.

stories.text: Renardo Green leads the 49ers with four interceptions
stories.summary: The cornerback has 30 tackles, six passes defensed and a team-high four interceptions through eight games. A back injury has him questionable for Dallas, and Lenoir's foot injury leaves the secondary thin if both sit.

stories.text: 109.8: Brock Purdy's passer rating through eight games
stories.summary: Purdy has 1,980 passing yards, 17 touchdowns and five interceptions, and has been sacked eight times. Dak Prescott has a 95.3 rating with 14 sacks taken. San Francisco has won the last four meetings and leads the all-time series 21-19-1.

stories.text: At Dallas Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The 49ers (7-1) lead the NFC West by 2.5 games and visit AT&T Stadium. Watch how the offense adjusts without Evans and whether Williams plays. Dallas is 4-5 and scores 27.3 points per game.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Drew Lock starts again at Las Vegas

stories.text: Drew Lock starts again while Sam Darnold heals
stories.summary: Mike Macdonald said Lock will start Sunday at Las Vegas and that the fill-in stint lasts at least one more week. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of the loss to Chicago and later hurt his quad. He is week-to-week, not on injured reserve, and may return after the Week 11 bye. Lock threw for 175 yards and a touchdown in the 17-3 win over Arizona with no turnovers.

stories.text: Quenton Nelson out, Leonard Williams and Nwosu questionable
stories.summary: Nelson, acquired from Indianapolis on Oct. 27, will miss the Raiders game after a knee procedure and is week-to-week. Leonard Williams, Brandon Pili, Rashid Shaheed and Uchenna Nwosu carried questionable tags on the early-week report. Lock has an oblique injury Macdonald called manageable.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba tops 1,000 receiving yards again
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba finished the Arizona win with 1,036 yards after nine games, making him the third Seahawk with three straight 1,000-yard seasons, joining Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent. Rookie back Jadarian Price led Seattle in receiving that day with 54 yards, the first time this season someone else topped Smith-Njigba.

stories.text: 11: straight Seahawks wins over Arizona, a franchise record
stories.summary: Seattle's 17-3 win ran its streak against the Cardinals to 11, the longest against one opponent in team history. The two meetings this season produced 10 combined points. Seattle also had no turnovers and allowed no sacks.

stories.text: At Las Vegas Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, then a bye
stories.summary: Seattle visits Allegiant Stadium to face Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick, in his first NFL start. Seattle's defense allows 4.1 yards per play, the NFL's lowest mark by 0.6. The Seahawks have their Week 11 bye next.
